#2227. Napoli-Lazio, trasferta vietata ai residenti nella Regione Lazio

Brutte notizie per la tifoseria biancoceleste. Dopo le recenti trasferte con esodi straordinari, tra le più sentite quella a Reggio Emilia con la presenza di circa 10mila laziali, arriva ora un aggiornamento rischia di frenare l'entusiasmo del popolo biancoceleste. In vista della prossima gara di campionato contro il Napoli, in programma domenica 8 novembre alle ore 12:30, è stato comunicato il divieto di trasferta per i sostenitori laziali, residenti nella Regione Lazio.

CLICCA QUI E SEGUI LAZIOPRESS.IT ANCHE SU INSTAGRAM

Una decisione che interrompe inevitabilmente la lunga serie di esodi dei tifosi laziali che hanno contraddistinto la stagione fino ad ora. Tuttavia, questa scelta non rappresenta di certo una novità: sono infatti già due anni consecutivi che viene emesso il divieto di trasferta per i tifosi biancocelesti al Maradona di Napoli.

La S.S. Lazio, in conformità alle informazioni ricevute dal Napoli Calcio, informa i tifosi biancocelesti che, in ottemperanza alle disposizioni delle Autorità competenti, i tagliandi del settore ospiti per la gara di campionato EniLive Napoli-Lazio, in programma domenica 8 novembre alle ore 12:30 allo stadio Maradona di Napoli, verranno messi in vendita secondo le seguenti modalità:

Modalità di vendita solo on-line: Circuito TicketOne.

· Capienza Settore: posti 2.482 denominato Settore Ospiti Superiore.

Da normativa vigente, il giorno della gara non saranno in vendita i tagliandi del Settore Ospiti.

#2226. Politano durissimo: "Siamo con Allegri. Ma non possono venire sempre gli italiani a chiedere scusa..."

Matteo Politano non le manda a dire, dopo il tonfo del Napoli contro il Porto. Queste le sue parole a Sky Sport: "Ogni tanto mi piacerebbe che venisse anche qualche altro compagno a dare le spiegazioni, non solo noi italiani. Ma va bene così, io ci metto la faccia come ho sempre fatto".

Non abbiamo visto i progressi sperati… "Assolutamente no, nel primo tempo avevamo anche approcciato bene, poi abbiamo subito tre calci d'angolo con due gol e una traversa dello stesso giocatore… c'è poco da spiegare, cose che non possiamo subire visto anche la stazza che abbiamo dietro".

Il gruppo è unito? Giusto affidarsi ancora ad Allegri? "Assolutamente non era un attacco verso nessuno. Siamo col mister, stiamo faticando ma dobbiamo raggrupparci. Ora abbiamo l'ultima partita, poi spero di recuperare qualche giocatore e che da lì possa iniziare il nostro campionato".

Perché il Napoli si scioglie nei secondi tempi? "Non lo so, ce lo siamo chiesti anche noi. A volte non è una questione di tattiva, perché siamo tutti dietro al pallone, ma manca la cattiveria e non c'è la sensazione di pericolo".

#2224. 5 novembre 2008, il Real Madrid ospita la Juventus. E Del Piero si prende una standing ovation

Il 5 novembre del 2008, a Madrid, c'è la Champions League. Fase a gironi con il Real che ospita la Juventus alla prima partecipazione dopo quello che è stato Calciopoli. E fa abbastanza bene, perché prima della sfida al Bernabeu ha raccolto sette punti in tre partite, tre dei quali proprio contro i Blancos nell'andata di qualche settimana prima.

Al diciassettesimo è già vantaggio Juventus, con Marchionni che ruba un pallone e poi serve Del Piero che di sinistro infila Casillas per lo zero a uno. Tante poi le occasioni per i padroni di casa con Sergio Ramos, van Nisterlooy, Raul e Diarra, autore di un errore clamoroso. Nella seconda frazione Raul chiede un rigore, ma è ancora Del Piero a giustiziare Casillas su punizione alla metà del secondo tempo, anche grazie a una barriera non posizionata nel migliore dei modi. Al novantaduesimo Ranieri decide di sostituire il capitano, con il Bernabeu che lo applaude a scena aperta.

#2222. Celtic's record transfer handed surprising ‘doesn’t matter’ goals verdict

Kasper Hogh has been told he can still have a major impact at Celtic even if the goals don’t start flowing.

The £11 million record signing has struggled to reproduce the form he showed at Bodo/Glimt, where he established himself as a major attacking threat.

But former Celtic star Vidar Riseth believes Hogh’s difficulties can partly be explained by the different role he is being asked to perform.

Riseth watched the Danish frontman flourish at Bodo/Glimt and feels his physical presence can be used to create opportunities for the players around him. He said: “Hogh is a big, strong target man. When he played for Bodo, they played a different style that worked for him. [SunSport]

“I think he’d like to get more crosses, as he did at Bodo, because he’s such a big lad with a good finish. Now they’re playing more up to him and asking to get the ball back again, so it’s different for him, but the most important thing for Martin is Celtic winning games.

Ex-Celtic star backs 'amazing' former boss to deliver amid growing pressure

Three Celtic summer signings named in B team XI to face Ross County

Celtic vs Hibs moved to new date as a result of Premier Sports Cup final

“If Martin wants to use Hogh as a way to give more space to other players, then that’s the best way to use him.”

Hogh showed his quality on the European stage during his time at Bodo/Glimt, scoring in Champions League victories over Manchester City and Atletico Madrid.

And Riseth insists the striker does not necessarily have to be the man finding the net to make a difference for Celtic. The Norwegian believes Hogh can occupy defenders and provide the space for his team-mates to make the telling contribution instead.

Riseth added: “Sometimes at Bodo he didn’t score the goals, but there’s always one or two defenders on him all the time. That gives space to the midfield and to other players to come through and score the goals.

“If he works hard and does a good job, it doesn’t matter who scores.”

#2221. Middlesbrough man to remain sidelined until December

Middlesbrough will remain without the midfielder until the start of December. That means he is set to sit out of their upcoming games against Wrexham, Watford, Bristol City, Swansea City and Southampton.

Pukstas, 22, joined Boro in the summer on a long-term contract from Hadjuk Split running until June 2031. However, he has featured only once for the Championship promotion hopefuls.

In this latest update regarding his condition, his head coach Hellberg has said, as per a report by The Northern Echo: “He’s a month away, maybe, something like that. He’s a strong boy, he came from playing a lot and now he’s doing everything to come back stronger in every way he can. That’s how you try always to look at things, you can work on the things you can work at and try be stronger at that.”

Middlesbrough are sat top of the table after their first 13 fixtures ahead of the likes of Birmingham City, Stoke City, Swansea City and West Brom as they look to claw themselves into the Premier League. They face Wrexham away on Wednesday night.

Middlesbrough signed Pukstas in the last transfer window to bolster their midfield department. He gives them more competition and depth in the middle of the park.

At the age of 22, he has bags of potential and the capacity to grow and develop down the line. In the meantime, he faces a tough battle getting into Hellberg’s starting XI.

The USA youth international has some strong competition for minutes in his position. Boro have the likes of Aidan Morris, Sebastian Berhalter and Riley McGree, among others, at their disposal.

Pukstas started out at Sporting Kansas City before switching to Hadjuk Split as a teenager. He went on to become a key player for the Croatian outfit and scored 27 goals in 138 games before Middlesbrough lured him over to England for a new challenge.

Middlesbrough are having to be patient with Pukstas at the moment. He has struggled with injury since his switch and hasn’t played as much as he would have liked.

He is young though and still has plenty of time left ahead of him at Boro. He can still play a key role when he is back available and fit again as the matches come thick and fast over the December to January period.

Hellberg’s men will be full of confidence at the moment as they aim to keep their momentum going and build a gap at the summit. They beat Charlton Athletic 3-0 at home last time out and will be hoping for something similar against Wrexham next up.

#2220. Allegri a SKY: “Abbiamo cercato di essere aggressivi, errori fatti in un momento di stanchezza”

Massimiliano Allegri, allenatore del Napoli, ha parlato a Sky Sport dopo la sconfitta contro il Porto in Champions League: “Devo gestire una situazione umorale e comportamentale nello spogliatoio? Ma no, non è questione di chi viene a parlare, stasera abbiamo sbagliato sulle palle inattive e fino al 70′ per me ha fatto una buona partita. Abbiamo cercato di essere aggressivi, poi al 70′ abbiamo preso il secondo gol su una palla che rimbalza, saliamo per stanchezza dritti per dritti e prendiamo il terzo gol. Sono errori che in un momento di stanchezza possono esserci, in Europa i ritmi sono alti ma era già da minuti, dalla traversa, che ci infilavano facilmente e abbiamo preso due-tre imbucate con la Juve deciso di fare questa partita perchè era l’unico modo per difendere meglio, nel primo tempo non è andata male poi al 70′ in Champions loro hanno fatto cinque cambi e noi avevamo solo attaccanti. Per fare questo dispendio di energie devi avere dei cambi, altrimenti giochi vicino l’area e noi fatichiamo a difenderci. Abbiamo preso palla su rinvio nostro quando la partita era tranquilla. Nessuno in campo dice qualcosa ai compagni? Se riguardate il gol del 2-1, c’è un pallone che rimbalza con Beukema che sale dritto per dritto invece di marcare l’uomo alle spalle di Anguissa, c’è stata una disattenzione, è stato un dettaglio come a Torino con una partita tranquilla e Marianucci davanti ad Alajbegovic. Certi errori ti fanno perdere le partite. Alla prima partita conosco i limiti della squadra, a Genova mi è stato detto primo tempo brutto ma abbiamo gestito la partita. Poi però caliamo, oggi siamo numericamente corti. Oggi giochi ogni tre giorni, hai 7-8 minuti in più di gioco effettivo e al 70′ diventa un’altra partita e puoi gestirla solo con 8-9 giocatori in panchina”.

#2219. 14 milioni di euro per il capocannoniere della Champions League. Il miglior colpo dell'ultima estate per soli 6 milioni. Spendere non basta: le incredibili intuizioni del Como sul mercato

Anastasios Douvikas da Atene ha segnato contro il Lipsia, contro il Feyenoord, contro il Manchester United e lo ha rifatto, tre volte, pure contro il Lens. Adesso mette nel mirino Alessandro Del Piero che fece cinque reti consecutive in cinque gare di fila nei primi mesi con la Juventus. Nessun paragone, nessun s'indigni, ma Tasos è una delle tantissime lezioni del Como sul calciomercato. A tutte, che siano le ricchissime di Premier League, le snob di Spagna, le nobili talvolta cadude o decadute d'Italia. Douvikas è stato preso dal Celta Vigo, uno che faceva il titolare ma neanche sempre, era pure in panchina. Sedotto e abbandonato in Spagna, dopo esser stato magistrale pichichi in Olanda ma all'Utrecht. E che dire di Luis Milla: ogni innamorato del pallone, che mastichi tattica e sappia guardare oltre al gol spettacolare o al doppio passo, sa che uno così è un Sacro Graal per un allenatore. Ha trentadue anni e prima d'adesso era stato scartato dalle giovanili dell'Atletico Madrid e del Rayo, aveva girovagato nella provincia spagnola tra Alcorcon, Guijuelo, Fuenlabrada, Tenerife, Granada e Getafe. Con Cesc Fabregas è diventato un giocatore totale, mondiale.

La partita vinta, stravinta, dominata, conquistata ieri in Champions contro il Lens, è stata l'ennesimo manifesto ma mica quello definitivo. Il Como è un capolavoro in evoluzione e in rivoluzione d'idee. In un pallone dove sul mercato fin troppi gravitano attorno alle zone sicure, alle scialuppe di salvataggio, ecco che i lariani osano. Beninteso: lo fanno in una piazza dove non c'è pressione, dove tutto è gloria recente conquistata e allora anche il giovane riesce a performare meglio e con meno angoscia. Però Mirwan Suwarso e Charlie Ludi hanno saputo capire ogni pregio della propria realtà e sublimarla, sfruttando il loro algoritmo nativo del quale già parlavamo in passato. Scegliendo l'allenatore giusto, che sarà uno dei più forti al mondo come Cesc Fabregas, sul quale al momento abbiamo una sola domanda: perché dovrebbe andar via? Perché dovrebbe ascoltare altre sirene? Per andare in progetti senza direzione, senza cognizione di causa, che spendono e spandono e son fatti di troppe teste e zero raziocinio? Il Como è, alla prima volta in Champions, tra le prime otto. Tra le migliori del Mondo. E chissà che potrebbe accadere da qui a due anni...

Il Milan ha pagato 37,9 milioni Christopher Nkunku, il Como ne ha spesi 18 per Milan Baturina. L'Inter ne ha spesi 22,8 per Luis Henrique, il Como 6 per Alex Valle. La Juventus ha pagato 83 milioni per Lois Openda e Randal Kolo Muani, il Como 66 per Nico Paz. La Roma 23,5 milioni di euro per Neil El Aynaoui, il Como 750mila euro per Lucas da Cunha. 20 milioni al Girona dal Napoli per Miguel Gutierrez, 3,5 all'Herta Berlino del Como per Marc-Oliver Kempf. Potremmo andar avanti a lungo, pensiamo a quali colpi il Como non ha azzeccato negli ultimi anni. Alvaro Morata, dite? Sentite cosa dicono i giocatori dello spogliatoio, di lui. "Abbiamo pianto, quando è andato via". C'è stato anche questo, non solo i gol (mancati), nell'era di Alvaro. Non sembri normale quel che ha fatto ieri la formazione di Fabregas. E' un capolavoro destinato a restare, e poco importa se il Lens ha abbandonato la barca al largo dopo un tempo di gara. Abbiamo una grande squadra europea. Occhio...

#2218. Celtic learn match officials for Besiktas and Kilmarnock home double-header

Match officials have been confirmed for Celtic’s upcoming clashes with Besiktas and Kilmarnock.

Celtic face the Turkish side at Celtic Park in the Europa League before returning to Premiership duty against Kilmarnock in Glasgow.

German referee Sascha Stegemann will take charge of Celtic’s meeting with Besiktas. He will be assisted by fellow Germans Christof Gunsch and Marco Achmuller, with Martin Petersen appointed as the fourth official. Benjamin Brand will be on VAR duty, assisted by Patrick Hanslbauer.

Stegemann has previously been involved in a Celtic game, although he has not refereed Celtic from the middle. He was in charge of VAR when Celtic drew 0-0 away to Dinamo Zagreb in the Champions League in December 2024.

Celtic's record transfer handed surprising ‘doesn’t matter’ goals verdict

Ex-Celtic star backs 'amazing' former boss to deliver amid growing pressure

Celtic vs Hibs moved to new date as a result of Premier Sports Cup final

Celtic will then turn their attention back to domestic action when Kilmarnock visit Celtic Park on Sunday, November 8.

The Premiership clash kicks off at 4pm, and John Beaton has been appointed as the man in the middle. David Roome and Gordon McCabe will run the lines, with Colin Steven acting as the fourth official. Grant Irvine will oversee VAR, assisted by Dan McFarlane.

It will be Beaton’s second Celtic appointment of the 2026/27 season. His first was the Glasgow Derby against Rangers at Celtic Park.

Last season, Beaton refereed seven Celtic league matches, with Celtic winning five, drawing one and losing one.

Those victories came against Aberdeen, Kilmarnock, Falkirk and twice against Motherwell. Celtic drew 2-2 away to Rangers, while their only defeat was a 2-1 loss at Dundee United.

#2217. Scott Parker’s first West Ham starting XI predicted as Cardiff City clash awaits – Tomas Soucek in

West Ham have acted quickly to replace the sacked Nuno Espirito Santo, naming Scott Parker as their new head coach on Wednesday morning. The former WHUFC captain jumps straight into the action too, as he will lead his new club in the clash with Cardiff City later tonight.

Parker will be backed by a first-team coaching staff including Steve Potts, Gerard Prenderville and Mark Noble, who have overseen preparations for the clash with the Bluebirds.

The new boss will need time to work out his strongest starting XI as he gets to grips with the squad at his disposal. However, his first lineup against Cardiff City could see some welcome reintroductions.

Hermansen; Veltman, Mavropanos, Kilman, Morato; Engels, Soucek; Bowen, Kante, Austbo; Piroe.

Parker has primarily played with a 4-2-3-1 formation over his managerial career to date. It is the system West Ham played in under Nuno too, so for the sake of continuity given the lack of time on the training ground under the new boss, it seems inevitable that they start in this setup against Cardiff City.

The new boss prefers his goalkeepers to be proficient in possession, as shown by James Trafford’s success in his Burnley team. As such, Mads Hermansen should keep his place ahead of Alphonse Areola despite recent questions over the Dane’s form.

Kyle Walker-Peters limped off in the defeat to West Brom, so Joel Veltman should start. Morato continues on the left flank, but in a big boost, Konstantinos Mavropanos may return in place of Airidas Golambeckis as he trained on Monday ahead of the game. If he is not fit though, the youngster will keep his spot.

In midfield, Tomas Soucek replacing Divine Mukasa seems a smart move to give Parker and WHUFC a bit more experience and physicality in midfield. He will partner Arne Engels, and Mohamadou Kante should retain his place in a more advanced roles.

Captain Jarrod Bowen is a shoo-in for a start on the right, and on the left, it’s a toss-up between Edvin Austbo and Manor Solomon. The latter is struggling for form though, so could be benched again.

Up top, Joel Piroe could be the proven Championship goalscorer Parker needs. He has Taty Castellanos and Pablo to pick from too.

It is a rarity to see a head coach appointed and lead their first game on the same day. However, Parker is wasting no time in getting to work with his new West Ham group.

He will lean on his coaching staff for the first game, before likely taking on a more leading role in team selection when WHUFC face Blackburn Rovers on Saturday. Parker will have had more time to assess his players and should have a better idea of who he wants in his preferred lineup.

Cardiff City will pose a tough test, as they look to dominate possession and control their games. The Bluebirds are unbeaten at home, winning their last three on their own patch against Birmingham City, Watford and Charlton Athletic.

Tonight’s game kicks off at 19:45 and will be broadcast live on Sky Sports+.

#2216. Paulo Fonseca è il nuovo allenatore dello Sporting: contratto fino al 2030

Adesso è ufficiale: Paulo Fonseca è il nuovo allenatore dello Sporting CP. Il tecnico portoghese, 53 anni, prende il posto di Rui Borges sulla panchina dei Leões e firma un contratto valido fino al 30 giugno 2030. L'annuncio è arrivato attraverso un comunicato della società alla CMVM, nel quale è stata contestualmente confermata la fine del rapporto con il precedente allenatore e il suo staff.

Per assicurarsi Fonseca, il club di Lisbona ha raggiunto un accordo con il Lione sulla base di 5 milioni di euro. Insieme al nuovo allenatore si trasferiscono a Lisbona anche cinque componenti del suo staff: Paulo Jorge Martins Mourão, Nelson Diogo Vilas Boas Duarte, António Pedro da Silva Ferreira, Paulo Renato Rebocho Ferreira e Rui Jorge Azevedo de Faria. Anche per loro è previsto un accordo fino al 2030.

Per Fonseca si tratta di un ritorno in Portogallo a dieci anni dall'esperienza allo Sporting Braga, con cui aveva conquistato la Coppa nazionale nel 2015/16. Successivamente ha allenato Shakhtar Donetsk, Roma, Lilla, Milan e Lione. In Ucraina ha vissuto il periodo più vincente della carriera, conquistando tre campionati, tre Coppe nazionali e una Supercoppa. Ora lo attende la nuova avventura ad Alvalade, alla guida della squadra del suo cuore.

#2215. Napoli-Lazio, svelata la squadra arbitrale

Ufficializzate le designazioni per il lunch match delle 12:30: ecco tutti i direttori di gara scelti per la sfida.

In vista dell'imminente incontro di campionato tra Napoli e Lazio, fissato per le ore 12:30 di questa domenica, sono state ufficializzate le scelte della squadra arbitrale che guiderà la sfida. Il match sarà diretto dal fischietto torinese Luca Pairetto, un nome che evoca statisticamente un buon feeling per i tifosi laziali: nei 20 precedenti complessivi arbitrati dal fischietto piemontese, infatti, il bilancio sorride nettamente ai biancocelesti, con ben 13 vittorie, 3 pareggi e 4 sole sconfitte.

CLICCA QUI E SEGUI LAZIOPRESS.IT ANCHE SU INSTAGRAM

Il compito di arbitrare la partita è stato affidato a Luca Pairetto   Il direttore di gara sarà supportato lungo le fasce dai due assistenti Tegoni e Perrotti, mentre le funzioni di quarto ufficiale saranno svolte da Marinelli.

Per quanto riguarda la gestione della tecnologia a supporto del match, la sala VAR vedrà impegnato Aureliano come arbitro VAR principale, affiancato da Mazzoleni che ricoprirà il ruolo di AVAR.

#2214. Celtic B served an unflinching reality in defeat as big-name kids shown no mercy

Ross County boss Stuart Kettlewell reckons his side could have put Celtic's star-studded B team to the sword by an even bigger margin after booking their place in the next round of the KDM Evolution Trophy with a 2-0 win in Dingwall.

The Staggies boss knew his side would face a stern test against a Celtic second string packed with pedigree. £3million summer signing Joel van den Berg was handed his debut, while highly-rated Chelsea youngsters Landon Emenalo and Shim Mheuka also started.

But County proved too strong for their visitors and Kettlewell believes the scoreline flattered the young Hoops after a dominant display in the Highlands.

Speaking to Ross County TV, Kettlewell said: "It was a competitive game. We were a bit frustrated at half-time because we didn't feel we'd handled the ball particularly well and we didn't think we'd quite got our pressing right.

Read more: Celtic handed familiar whistler for Kilmarnock clash as European ref revealed

"We knew Celtic would be comfortable in possession and would look to retain the ball, but we felt there were more opportunities for us to turn it over.

"That said, we scored a brilliant goal in the first half. The run from Dean Cornelius, the cross from Lewis Jamieson and the finish was first class. We were really pleased with that.

"We also had three, four or five other good opportunities, hit the woodwork a couple of times and, despite not playing as well as we would have liked, still created plenty of chances while limiting Celtic to very little.

"I thought we were better in the second half. We won the ball back more often, had a bit more composure in possession and created a lot of opportunities.

"Their young goalkeeper made some outstanding saves and, on another night, we probably score a few more goals. We hit the woodwork again and had numerous efforts on goal.

"You have to give credit to Celtic. They're a young side, but they're a good side. They've brought in players from elsewhere and have talented homegrown players as well. We always knew it would be a good test and another challenge for us to solve in this competition."

Van den Berg's first outing since arriving from PSV offered an early glimpse of the highly-rated Dutch defender, while Chelsea duo Emenalo and Mheuka both got 72 minutes under their belts.

The trio are not part of Celtic's Europa League squad and therefore won't be involved against Besiktas, but they will hope their contributions in Dingwall have strengthened their case for a place in Martin O'Neill's plans ahead of Sunday's Premiership clash with Kilmarnock.

#2211. Jermain Defoe in line for coaching role with 46-year-old set to become Bromley boss

Bromley parted ways with Andy Woodman last month, in a controversial dismissal after five successful years in charge. Woodman had taken the side from the National League to League One, however, they have struggled this season and are bottom of the third tier table.

Byron Webster has been in charge on an interim basis. Now though, reporter Jason Burt states that Karl Robinson is set to join as the Ravens’ new manager.

Robinson has been without a job since June, following his departure from Salford City. He led the side to the League Two play-off final last season, losing out on promotion to Notts County.

Robinson, 46, is set to bring an assistant of his own with him to Hayes Lane, as Burt adds Jermain Defoe is poised to join alongside the new boss. He will serve as no.2 to the experienced manager following a maiden managerial stint of his own at Woking.

At the time of his first managerial appointment, Robinson was aged just 29 with MK Dons – the youngest boss in the EFL at the time. He spent six years with the Dons and has since managed Salford City, Charlton Athletic and Oxford United.

At each of his sides, aside from Charlton Athletic, Robinson has managed over 130 games. He averaged over 1.5 points per game at all of Salford, Oxford and MK, with his Addicks stint being the only exception again at 1.36 PPG.

Robinson often operates with a 3-4-1-2, but his vast experience has seen him switch systems and utilise four-man defences. He likes his sides to have high possession, with wide overloads, aggressive pressing and fluid midfield rotations.

A past shift to a 5-2-1-2 could be repeated at Bromley to provide them with more defensive solidity in their bid to secure League One survival.

In his time as a manager, Robinson has gained most of his experience in League One. He has won 796 points in the division, including 222 wins (Transfermarkt).

Defoe’s experience is more limited, but he is a budding coach determined to forge his way in the dugout after a short spell in charge of Woking. The former England striker has had roles at Tottenham Hotspur and Rangers alongside his stint with the Cardinals, and his experience as a top player could mean he has valuable nuggets of advice to offer to the players.

Bromley have mainly played in a 4-1-4-1 system this season, and it was regularly used last term alongside a 3-4-2-1. They may have to adjust to new demands under Robinson.

Bromley do not have a league fixture until November 21st now, but will hope Robinson can make an impression in cup matches against Rotherham United and MK Dons as he gets to work at Hayes Lane.

Robinson has the experience and tactical nous to bring success at Bromley, but time will tell whether the squad is truly strong enough to achieve such a feat after their quick ascent to League One.

#2210. Rangers learn match officials for Saturday night Premiership clash vs St Mirren

The match officials have been confirmed for Rangers’ Scottish Premiership trip to St Mirren.

Rangers travel to The Marbill Coaches Stadium on Saturday, November 7, with the league clash scheduled for an 8pm kick-off.

Nick Walsh has been appointed as the man in the middle, with Frank Connor and Daniel McFarlane running the lines. Gary Hanvidge will be the fourth official, while Greg Aitken is on VAR duty with Peter Stuart assisting.

This won't be Walsh’s first involvement with Rangers this season. He took charge of the Premier Sports Cup clash between Rangers and Celtic at Ibrox in September, which Rangers won 3-0.

Rangers hero 'set' for new role at EFL side after leaving last club over summer

Why Sebastien Pocognoli picked James Penrice as he talks up Rangers star's quality

Rangers game rescheduled as a result of Premier Sports Cup final participation

Walsh also refereed Rangers’ opening Premiership fixture of the campaign, a 1-1 draw away to Dundee United on July 31.

The experienced whistler had several Rangers assignments last season too. Those included a 1-1 draw away to St Mirren in August 2025, Rangers’ 2-0 League Cup victory over Hibernian, and the 3-1 League Cup defeat to Celtic at Hampden in November.

He was also in charge as Rangers lost 2-1 at Hearts in December, before overseeing their 2-0 home victory against Aberdeen in January.

Walsh later refereed the 3-1 defeat at Celtic Park in May.

#2209. Lazio, accordo Mizuno in scadenza: Napoli a 18 milioni più bonus

Il contratto tecnico biancoceleste si avvicina alla scadenza; quello del Como terminerà il 30 giugno 2027.

Il contratto della Lazio con Mizuno è in scadenza: per il club biancoceleste si aprirà la possibilità di chiedere una sponsorizzazione tecnica più generosa di quella attuale. Secondo quanto riportato da TuttoMercatoWeb, Il confronto passa anche dalle cifre del Napoli, che con Armani è arrivato a 18 milioni di euro più 2,5 di bonus.

CLICCA QUI E SEGUI LAZIOPRESS.IT ANCHE SU INSTAGRAM

L’intesa biancoceleste si avvicina alla conclusione in una fase in cui gli accordi tecnici dei club presentano valori molto diversi. Alla scadenza, la Lazio potrà puntare a condizioni economiche migliori rispetto a quelle previste dal contratto attuale.

Tra gli accordi richiamati nel confronto figurano anche quelli della Roma con Adidas e della Fiorentina con Joma. Le cifre dei due club offrono altri riferimenti accanto al contratto della Lazio.

Il Napoli ha rinnovato l’intesa con Armani dopo le prime stagioni da 9 milioni di euro più uno di bonus. Il nuovo accordo vale 18 milioni di parte fissa e altri 2,5 di bonus. Alla scadenza, prevista nel 2028 per l’intesa del 2023, è ritenuta probabile una revisione al rialzo, anche se resta da capire di quale entità. Aurelio De Laurentiis viene indicato come abile nell’ottenere condizioni favorevoli nei contratti commerciali.

Il quadro delle sponsorizzazioni entra in una nuova fase anche con l’accordo del Milan con Adidas: 500 milioni di euro in dieci anni a partire dal 2028. La Roma riceve invece 5 milioni più bonus dall’intesa con lo stesso marchio, una cifra giudicata bassa rispetto alle valutazioni degli altri club citati.

Per la Fiorentina, il contratto con Joma prevede complessivamente 20 milioni in cinque anni, pari a 4 milioni a stagione.

#2207. Furious Redknapp demands ex Rangers transfer chief is axed for transfer blunders

Former Rangers technical director Nils Koppen should have followed Nuno Espirito Santo out the door, according to Harry Redknapp, who claims incoming West Ham boss Scott Parker is inheriting the club's worst squad in more than 65 years.

The London club axed Nuno after a disappointing start to their Championship campaign, with Parker set to be unveiled as his successor on Wednesday. But Redknapp believes attention should also turn to former Rangers recruitment chief Koppen, who oversaw a major squad overhaul and is now facing questions over the quality of the players brought to the club.

And that includes Arne Engels, the former Celtic star was signed by the Hammers for £22m but has yet to fully convince.

Parker faces an immediate test with away trips to Cardiff City and Blackburn Rovers before the international break.

Read more: Rangers officials confirmed for Saturday night Premiership showdown

However, Redknapp reckons the former Fulham and Burnley boss is walking into an unenviable situation.

The 79-year-old, who joined West Ham as a 14-year-old before later managing the club, delivered a damning verdict on the current squad and insists those responsible for recruitment must be held accountable.

Speaking to talkSPORT, Redknapp said: "Scott's got a great track record of getting teams up from the Championship. He knows the club, he was a very, very good player for them and I took him from West Ham to Tottenham.

"He's a very astute manager and I think it's a great fit for West Ham.

"I think the first thing he needs to do, though, is have a look at this West Ham team. Honestly, looking back over all those years, this is probably the worst group of players I've seen at West Ham in that time.

"So he hasn't got a very easy job on his hands."

Redknapp then turned his attention to the club's transfer business.

"The manager gets the sack, but who is bringing the players in?" he said.

"I don't know Nuno, but one after another managers come in and go. If I owned that football club, I'd be looking at the people responsible for recruitment.

"Who brought these players in? Who spent all that money on bang-average players?

"Whoever is responsible for that should be gone with Nuno, in my opinion."

Redknapp believes Parker's chances of guiding West Ham back to the Premier League will hinge on improving recruitment.

"Recruitment is all-important," he added.

"You can only work with the tools you're given. Back in the day, managers signed their own players and if they were no good, you took the blame. If they were good, you took the credit.

"You need players who can play if you want to play good football. West Ham was called The Academy because they had incredible players.

"It's a fantastic football club that needs resurrecting. If Scott's the man, hopefully he can give them that lift. But I'd be looking very carefully at whoever is bringing the players in."

#2205. Three goals conceded: Ex-Sheffield Wednesday man endures a tough night on UEFA Champions League debut

Eyebrows will have been raised in both Sheffield and Rome when Devis Vasquez was picked to start for AS Roma in their UEFA Champions League clash against Manchester United on Tuesday night. The ex-Sheffield Wednesday loan man has served as backup ‘keeper in Mile Svilar’s absence, but came into the first XI at Old Trafford.

All was going well for former SWFC loan man Vasquez and Roma as they went 2-0 up within 17 minutes. However, the Colombian shot-stopper would concede three second-half goals as United fought back to win 3-2.

Vasquez made two saves but finished with an xG prevented of -0.50. having conceded three times from an xG of 2.50 (Fotmob). He was nearly a hero as he saved a penalty from Bruno Fernandes in the second half, but Roma’s Bryan Cristante was cruelly deemed to have encroached and the Manchester United man fired home the retake.

Vasquez was a 26-year-old goalkeeper on the books of AC Milan when he joined Sheffield Wednesday on loan in 2023. He came in and was the Owls’ starting no.1 under Xisco Munoz, but was dropped from the side after the Spaniard’s sacking and would never play for the club again.

The Long-serving Cameron Dawson stepped back into the starting role, before James Beadle joined in January. Vasquez was then recalled by Milan and promptly loaned out to Ascoli. Almost his entire time with I Rossoneri was spent out on temporary deals, and when he was released in 2025, Roma snapped him up.

Vasquez has served as cover while with Rome and did so in a half-season loan at Besiktas in 2025/26 too. He played once for the Turkish giants, keeping a clean sheet in a 0-0 draw with Fatih Karamguruk back in April.

Barring his loans to SWFC and second-tier Italian sides Ascoli and Empoli, Vasquez has mainly served as a cover option for all of his clubs. The now 28-year-old has the pride of making his UEFA Champions League debut though, despite the result.

Vasquez is looked back on as a fairly minor part of the Sheffield Wednesday side that endured dismal fortunes under Xisco Munoz. He didn’t give a great account of himself with a save percentage of only 59% while at Hillsborough (Fotmob), but the Owls had far bigger problems than their loan goalkeeper at the time as they went winless in their first 10 Championship games that season.

After the Colombian, the Owls had far better fortunes in the goalkeeping department. He was succeeded by loan hit Beadle in January, and the Brighton & Hove Albion prospect would return for the 2024/25 campaign.

The emergence of Pierce Charles would gather pace too, as he cemented himself as one of the UK’s brightest goalkeeping prospects despite shoulder injuries.

Now, as Vasquez earns opportunities with Roma, SWFC have Joe Lumley and Ashley Maynard-Brewer battling for the starting berth. The new ‘keepers will hope to play key roles under new boss Dave Challinor as the club rebuild after administration and relegation.

#2204. Lazio, Hernanes crede nella tenuta stagionale e avverte l’Inter

Per l’ex centrocampista, i biancocelesti giocano con intensità; i nerazzurri devono ritrovare energia e fare i conti con alcune assenze.

Hernanes ritiene che la Lazio possa mantenere il proprio rendimento per tutto il campionato. L’ex centrocampista brasiliano ne ha parlato a margine di un evento del Sigma World di Roma, commentando la prima parte di stagione biancoceleste. Secondo quanto riportato da Agipronews, Ha poi rivolto la sua attenzione all’Inter, che considera ancora la squadra più forte ma dalla quale si aspetta una reazione.

CLICCA QUI E SEGUI LAZIOPRESS.IT ANCHE SU INSTAGRAM

«La Lazio ha il potenziale per poter durare tutto il campionato», ha dichiarato Hernanes, secondo quanto riportato da Agipronews. Per il «Profeta», la squadra può contare su un allenatore vincente, che conosce la strada per la gloria e le ha trasmesso la propria onestà calcistica: scendere in campo dando tutto.

È questo, a suo giudizio, ciò che emerge dal gioco dei biancocelesti. Hernanes descrive una formazione intensa, con i valori giusti in ogni posizione, e sottolinea la qualità dei giocatori. «È una bellissima squadra che sta rendendo al 100%», ha aggiunto.

Parlando dell’altra sua ex squadra, Hernanes ha ricordato che nel calcio nessuna vittoria è acquisita prima di giocare: bisogna scendere in campo e dare il massimo. Pur ritenendo l’Inter la più forte, vede nei nerazzurri gli effetti della vittoria dello scorso anno. «Stanno ancora giocando con la pancia piena dopo la vittoria dello scorso anno», ha osservato.

Secondo il brasiliano, il calo di energia può avvenire inconsciamente. Finora, a suo avviso, l’energia impiegata era sufficiente; ora però l’Inter comincia a complicarsi la vita. Per questo, ha concluso il suo richiamo, i nerazzurri «devono svegliarsi».

#2203. Farioli a SKY: “Il gol del Napoli ci poteva tagliare le gambe, grande reazione nel secondo tempo”

rancesco Farioli, allenatore del Porto, ha parlato a Sky Sport dopo la vittoria contro il Napoli. “Siamo partiti forte, infatti abbiamo avuto tante occasioni sin dall’inizio. Abbiamo poi sbloccato la gara su palla inattiva e abbiamo avuto parecchie situazioni subito che potevano indirizzare il confronto, ma aver concesso 6-7 minuti a una squadra forte come il Napoli ci ha puniti, il gol subito poteva tagliarci le gambe ma la reazione del secondo tempo è stata fantastica sotto tanti punti di vista, come quello dell’intensità, della determinazione dell’aver concesso poco. Il risultato che arriva dopo tante ottime prestazioni. Avevo chiesto di dare seguito alle prestazioni che avevamo fatto ma con un po’ più di convinzione e fiducia, era nelle piccole cose che si poteva decidere A parte qualche errore, siamo stati bravi ad andare su palla, attaccare a testa bassa e abbiamo fatto tutto che dovevamo per giustificare questa vittoria Bruyne nell’area del Napoli, è servita tanta energia, tanta forza, quando gli azzurri venivano nell’uno contro uno e maggior controllo quando giocavamo nell’area avversaria. Abbiamo interpretato queste tre fasi con grande maturità. Negli ultimi due anni la squadra ha cambiato tanto, ma qui il calcio offensivo e di duelli fa parte del sangue e della storia del Porto: noi abbiamo cercato di riportare quello, di rimetterci quella determinazione e quella forza che ora ci stanno premiando. Sappiamo soffrire, sappiamo essere belli quando servono ma anche umili e lavoratori nei momenti duri: questo mi rende orgoglioso dei ragazzi, ma ora è comunque tempo di pensare al campionato, abbiamo una trasferta complicata”.

#2202. Hearts learn match officials for FC Thun and Falkirk double-header

Officials have been confirmed for Heart of Midlothian's upcoming clashes with FC Thun and Falkirk.

Hearts travel to Switzerland to face Thun at the Visana Stadion in the Conference League before returning to Premiership action against Falkirk at Tynecastle on Sunday.

Cypriot referee Kyriakos Athanasiou will take charge of the European encounter. He will be assisted by Marios Kalogirou and Kyriakos Sokratous, with Chrysovalantis Theouli appointed as the fourth official. Marios Christoforou will be on VAR duty, assisted by Dimitris Solomou.

Thursday's game is set to be Athanasiou’s first appointment involving Hearts. His previous European record also includes Conference League matches.

Hearts will then turn their attention back to domestic action when Falkirk visit Tynecastle on Sunday, November 8, for a 3pm kick-off.

Matthew MacDermid has been appointed as referee, with Chris Rae and Colin Drummond running the lines. Sean Murdoch will be the fourth official, while Steven McLean is on VAR duty and Gary Hilland will assist him.

MacDermid has previous experience of Hearts matches. He took charge of their 2-2 Premiership draw away to St Mirren in October 2025 before refereeing their 3-1 home victory over Motherwell in April.

#2201. Ospina dice basta a 38 anni: "Non volevo farlo ma devo ascoltare il mio corpo"

"Queste sono alcune parole che dedico al calcio dopo tanti giorni. Parole che non sono state facili, ma che sono accompagnate da tanta gratitudine". Comincia così il messaggio con cui David Ospina ha annunciato il suo addio al calcio giocato. Il portiere colombiano ripercorre le origini della sua passione: "In questi giorni ho ricordato il bambino che ero. Quello che alzò la mano quando l'allenatore chiese chi volesse andare in porta e fui l'unico a farlo. Quel giorno, sul campo del quartiere, decisi quale sarebbe stata la mia vita, anche se ancora non lo sapevo. Indossai i guanti e la realtà di ciò che potevo raggiungere diventò più grande dei sogni".

Ospina ha poi rivolto un pensiero ai suoi affetti più cari: "Grazie ai miei primi tifosi, mio padre Hernán, mia madre Lucía e mia sorella Daniela. Grazie a Jessi, l'amore che mi sostiene nei momenti difficili e condivide ogni vittoria con me. Grazie ai miei figli, che sono il mio trionfo più grande". Un ringraziamento anche alle squadre che hanno segnato la sua carriera: "Il Nacional, il mio debutto e il mio addio sono stati in verde. Nizza, dove ho capito che l'impegno porta le sue ricompense. Arsenal, luogo di leggende e anche mio. Napoli, una passione che non si spiega, si vive. Al Nassr, che mi ha accolto con esigenze e gioia. Atlas, che ha saputo credere in me".

Infine, il saluto alla Colombia: "Che privilegio e che immenso onore dare tutto per il mio Paese e cantare l'inno nazionale con migliaia di persone". La decisione non è stata semplice, ma il portiere ha spiegato le sue ragioni: "Non me ne vado perché lo voglio, lo faccio perché ascolto il mio corpo che mi parla. Queste parole sono la mia lettera d'addio da calciatore professionista. Non mi arrendo, mi sento grato. È stato un viaggio meraviglioso. Bambino, saprai guidarmi. Tu stai tranquillo, andrò dove mi porterà il sorriso".

#2200. Three goals from 1.27 xG: Sydie Peck defies the numbers to break seven-year Sheffield United duck

Sheffield United continued their fine form on Tuesday night as they defeated Preston North End 3-2 away from home. SUFC are now four games without defeat, and they’ve won four of their last six Championship matches.

It was a strong team performance from the Blades, but the man-of-the-match display from hat-trick hero Sydie Peck can not be overlooked. The 22-year-old midfielder scored three in the first half, becoming the first United player to score a competitive first-team hat-trick since Billy Sharp against Aston Villa in February 2019.

Peck did so from an expected goals (xG) of just 1.27 too. First, his cross bounced all the way through and beyond Daniel Iversen (0.02 xG) before he kept the Preston North End ‘keeper at bay and floated beyond a despairing defence for his second (0.21 xG). Finally, the Blades star slid in at the back post to convert from Romelle Donovan’s cross (0.81 xG) to seal his hat-trick.

Peck registered a total of 1.27 xG across his six shots – the most by anyone in the game. His attacking threat was emphasised by the fact his six touches in the opposition box was more than any other player too.

The Sheffield United man saw to his usual duties. He created two chances in total and completed 52 passes, also winning six out of seven aerial duels – a tally bettered by only Mark McGuinness in the SUFC side (Fotmob).

It was the complete midfield performance from Peck, who has grown in influence this season. His importance creatively is displayed by 21 chances created and 76 line-breaking passes, and 779 touches shows how regularly he is the man to get on the ball when the Blades have possession.

Peck has made 54 defensive contributions too though, winning 52 duels in total. This shows his willingness to get stuck in and do the dirty work, while 50 recoveries highlights his work rate as well (Fotmob).

Now on four goals this season, if Peck can start to score on a more consistent basis, he will really be a complete midfielder for Chris Wilder.

Peck has been with Sheffield United for over five years now, joining the academy after his exit from Arsenal. He broke into the team in the 2024/25 campaign and would grow in the 2025/26 season with five goals and five assists in 41 games across all competitions.

The London-born midfielder drew interest from West Ham in the summer, but he expressed a desire to pay back all those who have shown faith in him at Bramall Lane – including manager Wilder.

Peck is happy with SUFC and his continued improvements this season show his development isn’t being impacted by sticking around either. However, if he continues in his current form, interest is bound to grow, and exit opportunities will become more tempting.

Sheffield United are keen to renew Peck’s contract as his current deal runs out in 2028. It would be wise to strike an agreement sooner rather than later with clubs sure to be alerted by his impressive displays of late.

#2199. Lazio, Belahyane convocato dal Marocco: torna in nazionale dopo due anni

Il ct Mohamed Ouahbi ha inserito il centrocampista classe 2004 nella lista per le due sfide con il Niger.

Reda Belahyane torna tra i convocati del Marocco a circa due anni dalla precedente chiamata. Il commissario tecnico Mohamed Ouahbi ha inserito il centrocampista della Lazio nella lista per i prossimi impegni internazionali: una doppia sfida contro il Niger, valida per le qualificazioni alla Coppa d’Africa.

CLICCA QUI E SEGUI LAZIOPRESS.IT ANCHE SU INSTAGRAM

La convocazione riguarda il classe 2004, che in questo inizio di stagione ha trovato spazio e visibilità nella squadra capitolina. Le sue prestazioni hanno attirato l’attenzione dello staff tecnico marocchino e accompagnano il ritorno nella selezione nazionale.

La scelta di Ouahbi offre a Belahyane una nuova occasione per lavorare con il gruppo del Marocco. Il centrocampista potrà cercare ulteriore considerazione da parte dello staff tecnico, oltre a misurarsi fuori dal campionato italiano.

Il prossimo impegno della selezione marocchina sarà contro il Niger. Sono previste due partite nel percorso di qualificazione alla Coppa d’Africa, alle quali il Marocco potrà affrontare contando anche sul centrocampista biancoceleste.

Per Belahyane si tratta della possibilità di mostrare il proprio valore anche in nazionale. Dopo lo spazio conquistato con la Lazio, il ritorno tra i convocati gli permetterà di confrontarsi nuovamente con i compagni della selezione marocchina.

#2196. Hibs learn match officials for Saturday evening Aberdeen showdown

Officials have been confirmed for Hibernian’s Premiership trip to Aberdeen.

Hibs travel to Pittodrie on Saturday, November 7, with the league clash scheduled for a 5.45pm kick-off.

Duncan Nicolson has been appointed as the man in the middle, with Graeme Stewart and Christopher Gentles running the lines. Jamie Wilkie will be the fourth official, while Kevin Clancy is on VAR duty with Grant Irvine assisting.

It will not be Nicolson’s first involvement with Hibs this season. He took charge of their 1-0 League Cup victory over Partick Thistle at Easter Road in August.

Nicolson also refereed one Hibs match during the 2025/26 season, when the Easter Road side suffered a 2-0 Premiership defeat away to Motherwell in November. That encounter saw one red card as Motherwell claimed all three points at Fir Park.

Saturday’s appointment will therefore be Nicolson’s third Hibs match across the last two seasons.

The Aberdeen encounter will be Hibernian’s 12th Premiership fixture of the 2026/27 campaign.

#2195. How much West Ham paid to sack Nuno Espirito Santo after missing the chance to do it for free

West Ham made the decision to sack Nuno Espirito Santo on Monday, after a 3-1 home defeat to West Brom. WHUFC have acted quickly to hire Scott Parker as their new boss, but they had to pay a sizeable compensation fee to part ways with Nuno.

The Athletic states that the Hammers paid around £2m to relieve the Portuguese boss of his duties. This is after having the option to do so for nothing after their relegation from the Premier League was confirmed in May.

New manager Parker had the support of board members as early as May, before opting to stick by Nuno. Mark Noble was among the 46-year-old’s strongest backers but Dutch coach John Heitinga was also considered as a potential replacement.

As soon as the decision was made to stick by Nuno in the summer, the pressure was on for the West Ham boss. He failed to keep them in the Premier League, but there was hope he could get them back there having led Wolves to Championship promotion in impressive fashion in 2017/18.

There were encouraging signs, as the Hammers rose as high as top of the table during a run of 10 Championship games unbeaten. They scored for fun too, scoring 30 times in the first 11 matches, including big wins over Wrexham, Lincoln City (both 6-0), Derby County (3-0) and Wolves (4-2).

However, frustrations over the style of football continued with cautious play in possession persisting despite WHUFC’s star power in attack. Defensive concerns persisted too, and when the warning signs led to defeats against Southampton and west Ham, the crowd had turned on Nuno.

United are ultimately made to pay for sticking by Nuno in the summer – £2m to be exact. The appointment of Parker for nothing limits the expense of this managerial change, but when the Portuguese boss could have gone in the summer for nothing, it has proven to be a costly decision by the club.

West Ham’s appointment of Parker has led to a mixed response. Many are pleased to see a former Hammers star and three-time Championship promotion-winning manager join the club, but there are some reservations over his style of play.

Like Nuno, Parker’s tactics in recent jobs have been built on a solid defensive foundation, showing a willingness to let the opposition have the ball, and when his sides do have it, playing conservatively.

However, Parker has adapted his tactics over time. While in charge of Fulham, his side had the second-highest average possession in the Championship with 60.8% (Fotmob), and they went on to win the league. They also recorded the highest xG (90.4 – 20 more than any other team), most big chances created (136) and most touches in the opposition box (1,352).

It will be intriguing to see if Parker reverts to this, or sticks by the defence-first tactics that saw him win promotion with Burnley after conceding only 16 goals in 46 matches.

WHUFC supporters want promotion at any cost, but the criticisms of Nuno’s style of play suggest they would rather brings more forward-thinking and controlling football.

#2192. Porto, Farioli: "Raccolti i frutti di quanto seminato nelle prime partite, tre punti fondamentali"

Le parole di Francesco Farioli, tecnico del Porto, ai microfoni di Prime dopo la vittoria per 4-1 contro il Napoli. #2191. Farioli in conferenza stampa: “Il Napoli ha preparato la gara in maniera intelligente, match importante”

Francesco Farioli, allenatore del Porto, ha rilasciato alcune dichiarazioni in conferenza stampa dopo la vittoria in Champions League contro il Napoli:  “Il gioco è stato molto pesante, ci sono stati diversi momenti in cui siamo stati molto energetici e coraggiosi, soprattutto quando siamo andati a prendere la palla e loro ci pressavano, avevamo la giusta mentalità come i tifosi e questo ci ha aiutato ad avere la prestazione avuta. In ogni intervista ho detto che è stata una buona Champions ma non avevamo avuto punti, stavolta abbiamo raccolto i frutti. Questa vittoria è importante perchè ci servivano punti, sappiamo la storia del club e l’esigenza di fare bene in Champions League, di ottenere risultati. Una cosa non si può dire, che ci sia mancanza di volontà: ogni tre giorni abbiamo le giuste motivazioni, ci sono sempre gli avversari e le partite da giocare, e non sempre siamo al top della forma e a certi livelli la pressione si fa sentire. Dobbiamo imparare sulla nostra pelle, ci prendiamo i tre punti contro una squadra eccellente e ora vediamo le ultime quattro partite per guadagnare più punti possibili. La partita di stasera e i risultati hanno cambiato la prospettiva del match, abbiamo dovuto cambiare interpretazione del match e il coraggio dei ragazzi è stato notevole. Siamo stati bravissimi nella verticalizzazione e nel secondo tempo, l’impatto delle sostituzioni è stato fondamentale, chi è entrato ha contributo tanto. Cosa non è andato bene alla fine del primo tempo? In Champions ogni punto conta così come ogni gol può fare la differenza, stasera vincere con tre gol di differenza sicuramente è importante e ci aiuta ad avanzare, la performance dei ragazzi è stata eccellente. Le difficoltà del primo tempo? Non sapevamo cosa avrebbero fatto, avevamo preparato cinque scenari possibili e stasera abbiamo visto le scelte degli avversari con giocatori che non ci aspettavamo in campo. Abbiamo reagito bene e fatto la differenza. Come ho visto il Napoli? Non per dare meriti ai miei, ma il Napoli ha preparato la partita in maniera intelligente, quando ho visto la formazione ho pensato come potessero creare. La prima lettura è stata una scelta strategica e ben pensata in pochi minuti, abbiamo cercato di aggiustare le nuove dinamiche con l’ingresso di De Bruyne sotto punta, siamo stati bravi a portare dentro tanta energia, nel secondo tempo siamo venuti fuori con la condizione fisica e ritmo, chi è entrato ha alzato il ritmo ed è qualcosa in cui credo molto. Ho chiesto a Fofana e Gimenez di giocare fuoriruolo ma hanno avuto determinazione e spirito. Il calcio italiano? Le informazioni sono veloci e si può raffrontarsi con altre realtà, la Serie A la seguo da tifoso e da osservatore esterno, alcune dinamiche le conoscete meglio voi. Nuova onda degli allenatori toscani? Facciamo un lavoro bellissimo quando i risultati vanno bene, difficilissimo se la palla non entra. Spalletti ed Allegri sono dei riferimenti del calcio italiano, hanno portato innovazione nel ruolo dell’allenatore e ho un rispetto enorme per ciò che hanno fatto e continuano a fare. Su Alvini posso dire che è incredibile per lo spirito che ha il Frosinone, tanti anni fa andavo a vedere i suoi allenamenti al Tuttocuoio e ha sempre avuto una grande passione. Mi ha aperto le porte del suo centro sportivo per gli allenamenti e ancora non pensavo di allenare, ha un modo contagioso per come allena. Come abbiamo vinto? A fine primo tempo ho detto di avere ancora fiducia come nei primi 35′ di partita. Abbiamo avuto coraggio e alla lunga abbiamo meritato la vittoria, grande meriti ai ragazzi. Gabri Veiga aveva la febbre, aveva una faccia bianca stamattina e non aveva dormito: quando è uscito gli ho detto meglio fare così ogni partita. Ha grande intelligenza, conosce i momenti della gara e oltre a leggere il gioco aggiunge qualcosa di speciale come la sua fisicità strabordante come volume ed esplosività. Ha ancora grandi margini di miglioramento sulla continuità, sta migliorando e rispetto al suo percorso ha voglia di fare tanto e bene. Poi tra cinque anni chissà, per ora ce lo godiamo. Occasione per un italiano all’estero prima di tornare in Italia? A volte non danno e a volte non si prendono le opportunità, ci sono momenti: negli ultimi due anni e mezzo ho lavorato per club con sale piene di trofei. Lavorare assieme come succede al Porto poi ti rende difficile guardare altrove, sono felice qui: è la realtà, sono felice di lavorare con un gruppo straordinario e con le persone che rappresentano il club e fanno di tutto per il club, creativi nel cercare soluzioni nei momenti di difficoltà. Abbiamo tante partite da giocare, testa bassa e pedalare”.

#2190. Ex-Celtic star suffers major injury scare just hours after Scotland call

Former Celtic defender Stephen Welsh has handed Scotland boss Sebastien Pocognoli an injury scare just hours after being named in his latest squad.

The Swansea City centre-back was forced off after only 24 minutes of his side’s clash away to Portsmouth following a late challenge from Ebou Adams.

Welsh needed assistance from two members of the Swansea medical team as he made his way off the pitch, raising concerns over his availability for Scotland’s upcoming Nations League double-header against North Macedonia and Switzerland.

The 26-year-old was included in Pocognoli’s squad earlier in the day, with the Scotland boss also welcoming several established names back into his group, including Scott McTominay.

Celtic vs Besiktas: TV channel, live stream and kick-off time

Ex-Celtic star’s £22m move takes fresh twist as manager who signed him axed

Rangers-daft pundit sounds Celtic alarm with ‘Covid year’ warning

However, Welsh’s injury could now force Pocognoli into making a change before his squad even meets up.

Swansea boss Vitor Matos admitted after the game that there is a possibility the injury could prove serious, with the defender set to undergo a scan.

Asked about Welsh’s condition, Matos said: “Of course there is that possibility, but let’s first have the scan and then speak about it.”

Welsh has been an ever-present for Swansea this season and has also established himself in the Scotland set-up.

The former Celtic man earned his first senior cap against Slovenia during the previous international camp before featuring in all of Scotland’s matches during that break.

He now has four appearances for his country, but Scotland will face an anxious wait over his fitness ahead of the meetings with North Macedonia and Switzerland.

#2189. Three games, three goals, three wins: Midfield maverick stars again as Norwich City thrash Derby County

Norwich City cruised past Derby County with much of the hard work done by half time. NCFC were 3-0 up at the break, and Jovon Makama lashed home a stunning striker to seal the victory in the second half.

It was another strong team performance for the Canaries, as displayed by the fact there were four different goalscorers. However, one man who stood out and got himself on the scoresheet once again was attacking midfielder Paris Maghoma.

Maghoma had Rams midfielder Alex Mowatt biting on every dummy before he fired home from outside the box for the Canaries’ second goal of the night. It made it three goals in three consecutive wins for the maverick playmaker, who looks to be back at his best.

Maghoma made an impression early on in his Norwich City career, scoring in his first starts in the FA Cup and Championship after joining in January. His trickery and flair has frustrated even manager Philippe Clement at times, but it isn’t easy to curtail someone as expressive and skilful as the 25-year-old.

The attacking midfielder was influential in the Derby County win. Alongside his goal, Maghoma created one chance and one big chance, also completed five passes into the final third (Fotmob).

Maghoma had only started two Championship games before his recent three-game scoring and starting run. His per 90 stats show just how impactful he has been when on the pitch though, offering a creative streak and valuable abilities in progressing the ball through passes and dribbling.

Across his 442 league minutes, the NCFC ace is averaging 2.44 chances created, 6.11 line-breaking passes, 57.83 touches and a 60% dribble success rate per 90. His three goals from 10 shots and just 0.87 xG shows how clinical he has been when given an opportunity at goal too – although that does beg the question whether such goalscoring form will continue (all stats via Fotmob).

Maghoma has been a standout player in Norwich City’s three-game winning run, and there will be confidence that he can continue in this vein. However, both he and the entire team face a challenge in the effort to maintain their form.

The last three games have been against Derby County, Watford and Charlton Athletic – three of the league’s worst form teams. If NCFC are to keep pushing up the table and come good on their promotion ambitions, they have to maintain these high standards against tougher opposition.

A trip to Michael Skubala’s Bristol City marks a step up for the Canaries, but it is another winnable match. It would be a real morale boost to enter the upcoming international break off the back of four wins, and Maghoma’s recent form indicates he will have a key part to play in continuing the run.

#2188. Palermo, Inzaghi fermato da una tonsillite: ci sarà ad Ascoli? Intanto Pierozzi è stato operato

Come fa sapere il Palermo mediante una nota ufficiale, nella giornata da poco trascorsa, quella di mercoledì 4 novembre, è proseguita la preparazione della squadra in vista della sfida in quel di Ascoli, ma la seduta è stata guidata dall’allenatore in seconda Maurizio D’Angelo, che ha sostituito il tecnico Filippo Inzaghi, fermato da una tonsillite che non gli ha consentito di essere in campo. #2187. Scotland on alert as Slovenia rocked by fan mutiny before crunch Nations League clash

Slovenia boss Bostjan Cesar has pleaded with their own fans to behave after a bizarre threat by Maribor supporters to disrupt their huge game with Switzerland in Scotland's Nations League group.

Scotland will be paying close attention to the other game in the group when Sebastien Pocognoli's side host North Macedonia a week on Friday, as they try and overhaul the Slovenians into second place in the section, after that damaging defeat at Hampden.

But the game between Slovenia and Switzerland is at the centre of a huge storm among the hosts.

Slovenia were originally due to play the game in Ljubljana, where they drew 0-0 with Scotland, but were forced to switch the game because of the poor state of the playing surface at the Stozice Stadium.

Read more: 'We must improve': Pocognoli spells out where Scotland have to up their game

They will now play for the first time in five years at the Ljudski vrt stadium in Maribor, but have run into a major obstacle.

NK Maribor's ultras - the Viole - have been engaged in a long-running dispute with the Slovenian FA following heavy disciplinary fines, protests and stadium bans.

And they have threatened to disrupt the game against the Swiss, which would lead to UEFA sanctions unless the Slovenian FA, the NSZ, close their South Stand section where they gather and leave it empty.

They unfurled a banner at the weekend which stated, 'NSZ the choice is yours: Close the stand or open your wallet.'

It provoked outrage in Slovenia and Cesar has urged fans to behave. He said: "I am a coach, so I cannot influence everything. But I believe that there will be no complications. I hope that real fans will come to support the national team, which has not played in Maribor for a long time.

"Let's make a positive story in Maribor and in the end we can all celebrate together.

"We have a great chance of getting second in the group, which was above our expectations at the start of the section."

And the Slovenian FA stated: "We hope and believe our national team will be welcome in Maribor and there will be no trouble."

#2186. Nathan Jones confirms worry over ‘tough’ injury setback for Charlton Athletic summer signing

Nathaniel Chalobah made his first start for Charlton Athletic since the end of August on Tuesday night. However, he only lasted until half time following a crunching challenge from Akin Famewo.

And, unfortunately for CAFC, it appears that the tackle aggravated the thigh injury that kept Chalobah out for two months. Speaking to South London Sport, Nathan Jones said: “He got injured. I think it is the same thing as what kept him out at the start of the season – his thigh.

“We will have the diagnosis, but it wasn’t a tactical decision, we won every game with him at the start of the season and then he got injured. We tried to bring him back – he has trained with us for nearly two weeks so it is not too early. We were always going to give him 55-60 minutes anyway, but I think he has pulled his thigh. It is a tough one again.“

Chalobah’s last start came against Preston North End, a game Charlton Athletic won 1-0. The Addicks won their first three games of the season with the former Chelsea and Sheffield Wednesday man in midfield, but they have not won since.

Chalobah has gained a wealth of experience in the Championship, but he has often struggled with injuries. Previous club Sheffield Wednesday spent large spells without the 31-year-old, and the same fate looks to have hit the Addicks. He played only 31 times in a two-year stay at Hillsborough.

Chalobah’s most notable injury came during his time at Watford, when he had major knee surgery in 2018 and spent a total of 340 days sidelined.

Fears are that his injury struggles are set to persist at CAFC. His influence is clear to see as a strong defensive presence in the middle of the park, but the likes of Conor Coventry, Oliver Skipp and potentially the rarely-seen Timothy Ouma will have to cover in his absence.

In the summer, Charlton Athletic recruited some experienced Championship including midfielders Chalobah and Skipp. However, the former is dealing with injuries, and the latter is yet to win a game in CAFC colours.

They bolstered their forward line with Millenic Alli and Karlan Grant. Grant has scored two goals this season, however, Alli is yet to score and both are being outshone by academy graduate Tyreece Campbell – who has not scored in the last five league matches himself.

The Addicks need more from their summer signings, with disappointment over Chalobah’s lack of fitness and the limited impacts of bigger names like Grant, Skipp and more.

Charlton Athletic have some tough matches on the horizon, with Sheffield United, Wolves, Lincoln City and Blackburn Rovers to play before the end of the month. Time will tell just how long Chalobah faces out, but Jones has to find a winning formula with his available players, otherwise his future at The Valley will be in doubt as their winless run stretches to 11.

#2185. Leicester City must consider January action over £4m starlet’s loan if game time struggles continue: Opinion

Leicester City brought in Michael Golding from Chelsea for £4m in the summer of 2024 with the hope that he could grow into a first-team asset at the King Power Stadium. He had a strong youth career and a growing reputation at Chelsea, but has struggled to make the breakthrough at LCFC thus far.

Golding is only 20 though, and he’s out on his first senior loan with League Two side Shrewsbury Town. The Foxes will have hoped he could find regular minutes with Gavin Cowan’s side, but that has not been the case.

There are two months until the January transfer window opens, and it will be an important period for Golding. If his Shrewsbury Town loan continues how it has started, he could be recalled and relocated by Leicester City.

Golding moved to Shrewsbury Town late in the transfer window in August. Given his lack of senior experience to date, it was perhaps anticipated that the Leicester City prospect would need time to grow into a role at his temporary home.

However, with over a quarter of the League Two campaign down, Golding has played only 115 minutes of fourth-tier football for Salop. He has been used off the bench in the last two games after being unused against Bristol Rovers and Crawley Town, although that was off the back of an absence through injury.

The LCFC loanee gave a taste of what he can offer with a first senior goal in a 2-1 EFL Trophy win over Everton’s U21s last month. However, other players have been favoured in midfield with all of Tom Sang, Isaac Fletcher, Will Gray and Jay Turner-Cooke finding more minutes than Golding.

As he rebuilds his fitness after an injury, it will be hoped he can gain momentum and find more opportunities. As of yet though, chances have been few and far between in League Two.

Golding has impressed in the Leicester City academy with four goals and three assists in 40 games for the U21s. He has only one first-team appearance to his name but still has plenty of time to maximise his potential at only 20.

However, he needs game time to develop and show how good he can grow to be. If Shrewsbury Town aren’t going to offer him meaningful opportunities, LCFC will have to consider recalling Golding in January.

This is a key season for the midfielder’s future, as he will have only one year left on his deal when his Salop stay is currently scheduled to end in the summer. At that point, the Foxes will have to decide whether to renew his contract, or potentially sell him to recoup a fee.

Golding’s 2026/27 campaign will prove decisive in this. If he can show progress on the senior stage, he could earn more time to fight for a place in Russell Martin‘s future plans.

#2184. 45-cap Rangers star left out for Scotland clash as national boss reveals reason

Bojan Miovski has been ditched by North Macedonia for their Nations League game in Scotland after manager Goce Sedloski confirmed it was due to his lack of playing time at Rangers.

The 27-year-old has been a key man for his national team since making his debut five years ago and has won 45 caps.

However, he's been relegated to a bit-part player at Rangers under Derek McInnes and has played a total of just 72 minutes all season for the Ibrox club.

The former Girona hitman has made eight appearances off the bench, mostly for very short periods, although he did net a vital last-gasp winner against St Mirren in September for his only goal of the season.

But despite featuring for North Macedonia in all four Nations League games, including starting the 2-0 defeat to Scotland in Skopje, he wasn't included in their squad for their final two games... including one at Hampden.

Rangers learn match officials for Saturday night Premiership clash vs St Mirren

Rangers hero 'set' for new role at EFL side after leaving last club over summer

Why Sebastien Pocognoli picked James Penrice as he talks up Rangers star's quality

Sedloski said: "Miovski has not had playing time at Glasgow Rangers for a long time; that's why I decided on the four strikers I selected. He has not been deleted from the squad - when he has more playing time and when he plays, he will get a call-up.

"There is no anger about the decision. I have always decided to select those who are playing, and I will continue that way. Those who do not play in the teams will not be called up. Let's fix the mistakes we made here against Scotland.

"We are playing against a strong team like Scotland, and we need to forget about our recent form and give everything."

North Macedonia have not scored for eight games and failed to win a match in their last dozen games.

#2183. Portsmouth must take action over 22-year-old’s League One loan as Mousinho confirms clear ‘need’: Opinion

Portsmouth signed Hayden Matthews as a highly-rated centre-back prospect in the winter of 2025. He had emerged as one to watch at Sydney FC and quickly made a good impression at Pompey too, with his performance away at Oxford United in the 2024/25 season one fondly remembered.

But, Matthews was loaned to Bradford City for the 2025/26 season after a string of injury blows and centre-back signings. Unfortunately, the 22-year-old has struggled for minutes at Valley Parade, and manager John Mousinho has stressed his need for game time.

Speaking to The News on Matthews’ situation, Mousinho said earlier in November: “He’s gone out on loan with every intention to play, but unfortunately Bradford’s (defensive) record is one of the best in the country. We’ll see what happens – they (Matthews and Josh Knight at Reading) need to play.”

Matthews is a highly promising centre-back. His time at Portsmouth has been disrupted, but there are few doubts over his potential having displayed his composure on the ball, progressive abilities in possession and knack for reading the game.

A loan to Bradford City felt ideal, allowing Matthews to play in a solid defensive setup at a level that would require him to develop his physical game. However, he didn’t get any opportunities under Graham Alexander, and his struggles have continued under Michael Duff too.

All of George Pratt, Macaulay Gillesphey, Aden Baldwin, Reece Welch and Matthew Pennington have ranked ahead of Matthews in the pecking order. Given that they have kept nine clean sheets and conceded only eight goals in 13 League One matches, it seems unlikely that the setup is changed to make way for the Pompey loan man.

Portsmouth can not allow this to continue for the entire season, and Mousinho’s words suggest they won’t. Barring a miraculous turnaround, the Championship side must take action and recall Matthews this winter.

Matthews’ Bradford City stay has not gone as hoped, and his struggle for game time may seem like a put-off for some admirers. However, the Portsmouth man is clearly a talented defender, and he has plenty of room to grow with meaningful minutes in the right setup.

It means that other League One clubs should not hesitate to move for Matthews when Pompey recall him. Ideally, he can play in a team similar to Bradford City, who prioritise a strong defensive base.

That will ensure Matthews has plenty of opportunities to develop the areas of his game he needs to focus on.

Matthews is under contract at Fratton Park until 2029, and there is still scope for him to forge a future at the Championship side. However, finding minutes to grow as a player is a must for 2027.

#2182. Your 'loud and crazy' supporters won't stop us winning at Celtic Park

Former Arsenal star Leandro Trossard has warned Celtic that Besiktas are coming to Parkhead determined to take three points.

The Belgian international believes his side can handle the famous Celtic Park atmosphere as they look to continue their impressive Europa League campaign. Trossard joined the Turkish giants from Arsenal in the summer and has set his sights on going deep into the competition.

Celtic are still searching for their first points of the league phase following a defeat to Celta Vigo last time out, while Besiktas have enjoyed a strong start.

And Trossard insists the visitors will not be intimidated by the Parkhead crowd. He said: “We want to get three points from the Celtic match. It will be very tough. They have loud and crazy fans, but if we can translate what we want onto the pitch, then we will win. [SunSport]

Trossard believes there is even more to come as they target a place among the Europa League’s top eight. He added: “I’m very excited and we want to reach the top in Europe. The decisive factor is the draw and the team’s performance during these next few games.

#2181. Manchester United confirmed lineup: Amad & Yoro return to starting lineup

Shumail Sajid writes about Manchester United for Read Man Utd and Crystal Palace for Read Crystal Palace, with occasional pieces on other Premier League clubs. He has also written for FanSided's Red Devils Dispatch, Yardbarker, Anfield Central and The Sports Side.

Manchester United and Tottenham Hotspur return from the international break with plenty to prove when they meet at Old Trafford on Saturday.

Michael Carrick’s side have won just once in their last four domestic matches since beating Ipswich 5-2. A Carabao Cup defeat to Brighton was followed by a loss to 10-man Manchester City, before Manchester United drew with Everton and Fulham. Matheus Cunha’s late equaliser at Fulham rescued a point, but Manchester United still sit 12th.

Roberto De Zerbi’s side are bottom of the Premier League with only two points from their opening five games. Spurs have failed to score in four of those matches, while defeats against Aston Villa and Newcastle have added to the pressure.

Michael Carrick has named his starting eleven for the clash at Old Trafford, with Kobbie Mainoo and Youri Tielemans partnering in midfield as United look to get their season back on track.

Senne Lammens starts in goal, with Leny Yoro, Lisandro Martinez, Harry Maguire and Luke Shaw forming the back four. Carrick has opted for Mainoo and Tielemans in the middle, with Amad Diallo, Bruno Fernandes and Matheus Cunha tasked with supporting Bryan Mbeumo up front.

Leny Yoro had a brilliant international break where he made his debut for France. His performance on debut was enough for Zidane to praise the debutant.

Amad, after missing the start of the season with an injury, returns straightaway to the team.

Carlos Baleba starts on the bench and is expected to make his debut today. Marcus Rashford is also on the bench alongside Shea Lacey.

Lammens; Yoro, Martinez, Maguire, Shaw; Mainoo, Tielemans; Amad, Bruno Fernandes, Mbeumo; Cunha.

Mbeumo gets his place through the middle, while Amad and Cunha start on the wing after scoring the late equaliser against Fulham. Fernandes will be expected to start producing the numbers from last season after a lackluster start to the season, except against Ipswich, before the international break.

United need a response after a difficult run, but Tottenham arrive under pressure of their own. With both sides desperate for points, the starting lineups set the stage for an important afternoon at Old Trafford.
