#2051. Cardiff City 3 – 3 West Ham | Final whistle, first impressions

IT took all of eleven minutes for the new manager bubble to burst as the home side opened the scoring and the Cardiff City fans duly launched into ‘you’re getting sacked in the morning’ to welcome West Ham’s Scott Parker into the dugout. To be fair, a cracking strike from Jack Moylan gave Hermansen no chance and as is now customary, the Hammers found themselves playing catch up.

Parker’s West Ham had set up with a back four holding a surprisingly high line, plus Magassa and Engels playing in front of the defenders but the pair were still bisected by the excellent pass that put Moylan through for his goal.

New manager, same misery as three went in before half time – again

Magassa and Kilman went into the book early on, the young Frenchman in particular looking short of match pace. Taty looked isolated – as we’d feared – and the Hammers looked a little short of ideas the half hour mark, hardly venturing into their opponent’s 18 yard box.

The warning signs were there as the awful Morato was beaten a couple of times as the Bluebirds attacked down the left: The stand in left back duly gave away a penalty, again out of position and clambering all over the back of his winger. Two-nil with Hermansen again beaten from a spot kick.

A third came from a corner, headed in at the near post by Moylan – a hat trick in the first half – and Scott Parker might have been questioning his rush to assume control ahead of the international break: Three nil before half time, three goals conceded for a third week in a row and the Hammers booed off by their own fans again.

Piroe warming up with Kanté and Mayers showed three changes at half time as Magassa, Morato and Taty departed.

Mukasa’s lobbed goal after being put through by Bowen put the Irons back in the game, with still half an hour to go and at least giving the travelling supporters something to cheer. Bowen, playing more centrally, started to pull the strings and Piroe went close. Suddenly, from nothing, a Bowen through pass was flicked on by Piroe and Engles, through on goal slotted home like a veteran striker. 3-2: And thousands of Hammers armchair fans were thinking maybe, just maybe.

This was, at least, a fighting response to a half time dressing down and a well deserved barracking from the away fans.

Kanté almost levelled down one end, Hermansen inexplicably flew out and clattered Kilman down the other – almost giving away a fourth in the process- and suddenly, you couldn’t take your eyes off it.

And then – three – three and the roof came off thanks to Max Kilman’s goal from Bowen’s brilliant cross.

Absolutely chaotic scenes in the away end as the incredulous claret and blue army couldn’t believe they’d witnessed a fightback from a team dead and buried at half time.

It could have been four as Trott stretched his fingers to Soucek’s header – agonisingly close as the minutes ticked by. Brilliant second half efforts by Piroe, by Bowen – the man of the match – and excellent impact from Ezra Mayers who might just have found himself a role in Parker’s side.

Nuno’s team in the first half, Parker’s in the  second.

From the old Bobby Moore Upper to the Billy Bonds' stand these days - I've been watching since '03 and a supporter since about 1970.. Favourite player - Dean Ashton: Curse you Shaun Wright-Phillips. I still watch YouTube repeats of the Cup Final of 2006 hoping in vain that Shaka Hislop grows another six inches and stops Steven Gerrard's injury time equaliser. Can tell I'm getting old knowing I watched both Mark Noble's debut and his last game at West Ham. Pulling on a Claret and Blue replica shirt still makes me feel the same butterflies as when I was seven years old. Magic.

What I was particularly pleased about is that although we snatched a draw in spectacular fashion, there were no player celebrations, just long faces, no smiles. They know even this is not good enough. We are West Ham playing Cardiff in a half empty stadium. We should not struggle, we can not be happy with a draw under any circumstances. We need a winning mentality.

Maybe Jack Moylan is seriously good and we had not done our homework on Cardiff.

Lesson given and learnt then we started playing. Now just need to score three in both halves for the rest of our games and Scotty has done a good job.

How is kante not the first name on the team sheet after Bowen and mavropanos? He’s got everything and I really think the boy will have a distinguished career. Shocking first half, abysmal. Second half could have been more of a cricket score than a comeback. Utterly different halves of football. What I would say is austbo has to start and Solomon needs to look at himself. Not the finished article yet but the little Norwegian wants to make things happen. Anyone know if Alvarez is injured or just exiled?

Thank God he took Taty off, he has been coasting for a while now and Piroe showed his real worth, not wasting possession. always looking to play others in and a shot or two.

Mayers, at last playing at LB!! No problems defending, quick & physical enough to help down the left wing – really bright game.

Bowen, his best game of the season, ran the show, brilliant!

Thought Kilman should have come off at half-time – boy, was I wrong.

Fun seeing Noble and Parker after the match, constantly chatting, already planning, assessing, thinking ahead. Going to enjoy the ups and downs of the season knowing we have some wholehearted WHU stalwarts running the show.

Noticeable that our “strikers” failed to score, yet again ! What, exactly, does Castellanos get paid for ? Don’t get carried away by the second half performance. Just remember the first half & realize that we are a poor team, at the moment. You can’t simply give the opposition a big lead & then expect to be able to overcome them in the end. Typical West Ham performance: but WHY ?

#2050. ‘I hold my hands up’ - McAvennie issues fresh apology to Celtic star Auston Trusty

Frank McAvennie has issued a full apology to Auston Trusty and his family after admitting his initial response to criticism over comments about the Celtic defender “didn’t go far enough”.

The former Celtic striker faced an online backlash after questioning the length of time Trusty had been away from football following the death of his father.

McAvennie has now returned to the issue and said he is “genuinely sorry” for any hurt caused by his remarks.

In a fresh apology, he said: “Frank here. I’ve had more time to think about what I said about Auston on the podcast and I know my statement yesterday didn’t go far enough.

“I’m genuinely sorry for any hurt I’ve caused Auston or his family. That’s the last thing I’d ever want.

“I hold my hands up and I’ve learned my lesson.

“I genuinely wish Auston and his family all the very best.”

McAvennie's original comments came on his Let Me Be Frank podcast as he discussed Trusty's absence from the Celtic team.

He said: “I’ve got every respect for that, but how long do you want off?

“Martin (O’Neill) says he’s away to celebrate the life of his dad.

Hearts reveal investment in push for European return resulted in £2.4m loss Derek McInnes on Findlay Curtis Rangers future as he reveals player stance

“Celebrate the life? You’ve got football. You’re getting paid and we’re in trouble. How long is it going to be?

“It’s nonsense. My dad was the best man, the only man I looked up to, when he died.

Following criticism of those remarks, McAvennie initially acknowledged that he should have chosen his words more carefully.

He said: “I can understand why people feel my comments were insensitive, and looking back, I should have chosen my words more carefully.

“Everyone deals with grief differently, and I certainly meant no disrespect to Auston or his family.

“Celtic need the big man back, and that’s what I was clumsily trying to say.

“I wish him and his family all the very best.”

McAvennie has now conceded that statement did not adequately address his original remarks and offered a more direct apology to the Celtic defender and his family.

#2049. ‘Not good’ – Ally McCoist slams Liverpool star after mistake which left teammate ‘livid’

Ally McCoist was critical of one Liverpool player for his unwitting role in Fenerbahce’s equaliser against the Reds in the first half of their Champions League game on Wednesday.

The away side took a well-deserved lead in the 25th minute when Trey Nyoni’s deflected shot sailed into the net, with the teenage midfielder being credited with his first official goal in senior football.

However, the hosts restored parity just four minutes later, and again it was with the aid of a deflection as Mason Greenwood’s free kick hit off Jeremy Jacquet and was diverted into the net, with Alisson Becker not disguising his rage at the defensive wall in front of him.

Speaking on co-commentary for TNT Sports (via BBC Sport), McCoist called out the French defender for turning his back on the ball as the set piece was struck.

The Scotsman said: “I think the goalkeeper will not be too happy with his wall. Alisson is livid. Jeremy Jacquet turns his back. You have to stand up and take it. Not good defending.”

Want more Empire of the Kop coverage? Add us as a preferred source on Google to your favourites list for news you can trust

The summer arrival from Rennes has been excellent in his time at Liverpool so far, rightly receiving plenty of praise for his performances and winning his first senior call-up for France, but he won’t be happy with his part in Greenwood’s rather fortuitous equaliser.

The normally teak-tough 21-year-old paid a heavy price for turning his back on the ball, even if nobody could legislate for the huge stroke of luck that Fenerbahce received.

He’s also met his physical match in Romelu Lukaku, with the Belgian striker standing up to Jacquet in a way that few (if any) Premier League forwards have managed since the start of this season.

If Liverpool were pegged back by a piece of brilliance which was near-impossible to defend, we’d be able to accept it, but the manner of Greenwood’s goal (and it had to be him, didn’t it?) will rankle as much with Andoni Iraola as it did with the visibly furious Alisson.

At the time of writing, hopefully the centre-back and his team can put that regrettable moment behind them and go on to take all three points home to Merseyside.

#2048. ‘Soft’ – Stephen Warnock takes aim at Liverpool star who ‘cost his side’ against Fenerbahce

Stephen Warnock was critical of one Liverpool player over the concession of a ‘soft goal’ in their Champions League clash against Fenerbahce on Wednesday.

The Reds had the lead twice at the Sukru Saracoglu Stadium, with Trey Nyoni and Alexander Isak netting for Andoni Iraola’s side, but the midfielder’s goal was swiftly cancelled out by a deflected Mason Greenwood free kick.

The home side equalised again through Archie Brown and had the final say with a Vedat Muriqi header which secured all three points.

The second Fenerbahce goal had Warnock pointing the finger of blame at Alisson Becker for not coming to claim the ball from the cross which led to the left-back’s leveller.

Speaking on MOTD: UEFA Champions League for BBC Sport, the former Liverpool defender said: “That’s another soft goal conceded by Liverpool but this one was more down to Alisson not coming to claim the ball – and either cleaning out Gakpo or letting him know he is coming.

“I just watched the replay and there was definitely no shout… that’s a lack of concentration from the goalkeeper, and it has cost his side.”

Want more Empire of the Kop coverage? Add us as a preferred source on Google to your favourites list for news you can trust

Alisson had bailed out his teammates a couple of times earlier in the match after some sloppy errors just outside the penalty area, but the goalkeeper won’t be happy with his involvement in Brown’s equaliser.

He was unusually hesitant in coming for the ball as the cross was played in, although he doesn’t bear sole culpability for a cheap goal for Fenerbahce.

Cody Gakpo was unlucky that his attempted headed clearance went backwards, but Dominik Szoboszlai completely switched off to allow the left-back to run in behind him and have a simple finish from close range.

It was a collective mess-up from Liverpool, who could also have done a lot more to prevent Muriqi from scoring what proved to be the winner for Dirk Kuyt’s side.

It’s now two defeats in a row to begin November for the Reds, but they’re still in a healthy position to advance to the round of 16 in the Champions League, having won their three previous games in the tournament.

#2047. Hearts get bad news on Calvin Miller in latest injury blow

Hearts boss Wouter Vrancken revealed Calvin Miller will require surgery on a knee injury that will keep him out for two months.

Both Tomas Magnusson and Miller came off during the first half of the Jambos’ 2-1 Premier Sports Cup semi-final defeat to Edinburgh rivals Hibernian at Barclays Hampden on Sunday.

The Iceland midfielder was taken to hospital with concussion and the former Celtic, Morton and Falkirk attacker left the national stadium on crutches and his knee in a brace.

Vrancken, who will be without 10 first-team players for the Conference League game against FC Thun on Thursday in Switzerland, was asked about Miller and said: “It will be two months, let’s say, depending on what the surgery says because it’s a meniscus injury.

“Tomas is doing good. The day after was already a lot better.

“There is a protocol, of course, with concussions. He will be for sure back after the (international) break.”

Vrancken will have to put together a side capable of getting a first win in the competition, after a 1-1 home draw against Nordsjaelland and a 2-0 defeat away to Trabzonspor.

‘I hold my hands up’ - McAvennie issues fresh apology to Celtic star Auston Trusty Hearts reveal investment in push for European return resulted in £2.4m loss

He said: “Yes, it’s a puzzle. I’m always happy to see that the players we work with and play out of position or talk with are always directly motivated to do it.

“They know how much they help the team by doing it.

“It’s good to see because they take responsibility and they don’t live by excuses.

“They have already done it for weeks. That’s how we also get good results and good performances.

“Now we have to try to do it two more times before the break.”

Vrancken is confident his side will respond positively to their defeat by Hibs in Glasgow.

He said: “I think so. They showed already a few times this season that they can bounce back in performance.

“I think when you leave out the last 20-25 minutes of the first half, we played a good game.

“It’s just a pity that we couldn’t reward ourselves in the second half with a goal that could spin it around.

“But I’m confident in the players that they are mentally ready to play the game.

“They (Thun) have a good team, they have a lot of energy, they have a lot of intensity. They have direct play, going fast forward a lot of moments.

“With a lot of energy, good quality players also in front.

“We will have to be spot on, we have to be on our level to make the result. But the aim is to try to get a win here.”

Yesterday evening, Gerry Cardinale was stopped by Carlo Pellegatti for an impromptu interview and he urged the AC Milan fans to ‘come together’.

Between the two defeats in the Europa League and the three draws in the league, it has been a so-so start to the season for Milan. In that sense, tonight’s derby against Inter could act as a catalyst for a good period, as a win would take them within four points of the Nerazzurri.

#2041. ‘They deserve it’ – Kostas Tsimikas admits familiar failing cost Liverpool in Istanbul

Kostas Tsimikas admitted that Liverpool got what they deserved in their 3-2 defeat to Fenerbahce in Istanbul on Wednesday.

The Reds were in front twice at the Sukru Saracoglu Stadium but still contrived to come away with nothing against Dirk Kuyt’s side, who claimed all three points thanks to Vedat Muriqi’s 79th-minute header.

Jeremy Jacquet was criticised for turning his back on Mason Greenwood’s free kick for the first equaliser, and Alisson Becker was culpable of poor positioning for Archie Brown’s goal to make it 2-2.

Speaking to UEFA.com after the match, Tsimikas magnanimously conceded that Fenerbahce were full value for their win and lamented Liverpool’s defending over the goals that they shipped.

The Greek defender said (via BBC Sport): “Congratulations to Fenerbahce, they deserve it. We didn’t play how we had to play. We didn’t defend after the goal we conceded. After three or four minutes, automatically we conceded another goal.

“I think we have to mark better if we want to win games. We didn’t play very good and that’s why we lost.”

Want more Empire of the Kop coverage? Add us as a preferred source on Google to your favourites list for news you can trust

It sums up how careless Liverpool were this evening that they were in the lead twice and occupied a winning position for only eight minutes against Fenerbahce, with the goals from Trey Nyoni and Alexander Isak cancelled out all too quickly.

The manner of all three goals that the home side scored will enrage Iraola – it wasn’t as though the Istanbul outfit had to produce moments of magic to inspire their way to victory over the Reds.

Tsimikas himself was far from convincing, enduring a ‘tough night’ in the words of Liverpool Echo reporter Paul Gorst as he struggled to contain the threat of Greenwood, and he ended up being substituted for Milos Kerkez with 15 minutes remaining.

Liverpool have now conceded 10 goals in their four Champions League matches, shipping three for the third European fixture in a row, a record which’ll surely concern the head coach at this phase of the competition.

The debrief from this game will not be a pleasant one, and a much better defensive performance will be required if the Reds are to return to winning ways against Crystal Palace on Sunday.

Unai Emery could soon put pen to paper on a new Aston Villa contract after the club dropped a big hint today.

The Spaniard has been simply sensational ever since stepping through the Villa Park doors in 2022.

That all culminated in Europa League glory last campaign and has continued with success to begin a new Champions League season.

As a result, no one has been surprised that links to Manchester United have been reignited.

That hasn't gone down well within the Villa hierarchy as Jamie Carragher was threatened with legal action for even suggesting it.

The claret and blue outfit have now made their stance clear, with all eyes now on a potential new contract for Emery.

The B6 faithful have never truly believed that their head coach would be on the way to Old Trafford.

With all the control that he has at Villa Park, it would be utterly bizarre for him to depart for the Red Devils.

Fans at Old Trafford don't seem to understand that.

Any noise now looks set to have been put to bed once and for all as Emery met with Nassef Sawiris on Wednesday.

Villa released a statement to X, reading: "Aston Villa held an important working meeting today to plan the club's future and lay the foundations for its long-term sporting and institutional project.

"The meeting brought together Nassef Sawiris, the club's Chairman and Unai Emery alongside President of Football Operations Roberto Olabe and Director of Football Operations Damian Vidagany.

Aston Villa held an important working meeting today to plan the club's future and lay the foundations for its long-term sporting and institutional project.The meeting brought together Nassef Sawiris, the club's Chairman and Unai Emery alongside President of Football Operations… pic.twitter.com/xDKbjHWvD7

"The discussions focused on jointly planning the club's long-term strategic direction, with positive discussions establishing a clear commitment beyond 2029 for the joint development of the club under the sporting leadership of Unai Emery based on the shared ambitions and common goal to reach excellency and keep growing during the next years.

"The objective is clear: to build an ambitious, competitive Aston Villa capable of taking on the biggest challenges and achievements."

That serves as a major hint that Emery could soon pen a new contract, but what could that mean for Manchester United?

This seems like a direct address from the Villans to the Red Devils.

It proves just the ambition that Sawiris has for the claret and blue outfit both on and off the pitch.

Emery is a major part of that and looks set to be sticking around for the foreseeable.

It isn't a new contract officially, but it is good as.

That leaves Man United without their favoured managerial target should they part ways with Michael Carrick.

It instead opens the door for the likes of Julian Nagelsmann or Eddie Howe to potentially move up the pecking order.

This is great news for Aston Villa and a bad day at Old Trafford.

#2036. Alisson rages at teammate, Dirk Kuyt in hot water - Four things you may have missed in Liverpool defeat to Fenerbahce

Senior Correspondent AUTHORITY Senior sports journalist with experience at GRV Media and VAVEL; University of Derby graduate. FOCUS Exclusive content, statistical analysis, and deep-dive reporting across the Breaking Media network. THE INSIGHT Max utilises a network of club and industry contacts to deliver verified, exclusive reporting and data-driven insight. He provides the intelligence behind the stories to ensure fans get the full picture.

Liverpool fell to a frustrating 3-2 defeat away to Fenerbahce on Wednesday.

A return to Champions League action was never going to be easy for the Reds at a tense Sukru Saracoglu Stadium.

The Fener fans were up for it from minute one and certainly made life difficult for the travelling outfit.

They were silenced early on as a deflected Trey Nyoni strike put Andoni Iraola's side ahead before Mason Greenwood levelled things just minutes later.

The second half followed a similar pattern as Alexander Isak made it 2-1, but flipped on its head when Archie Brown and Vedat Muriqi made it 3-2 by the 79th minute.

There was so much going on between Fenerbahce and Liverpool, here's some things that flew under the radar.

The Englishman may have gotten on the scoresheet with a deflected free-kick, but arguably should have picked up an earlier penalty.

Before Nyoni went on to give the Reds the lead, the ex-Manchester United man went over in the penalty area under pressure from Kostas Tsimikas.

Referee Clement Turpin waved away appeals, but when looking at a replay, it is clear that the Greece international pushed the attacker with two hands.

The hosts were well within their rights to demand a penalty, but VAR didn't even halt play for a check.

Commentators weren't even made aware that a check was happening, proving just how quickly this claim was resolved.

The above moment, fairly, left the hosts feeling let down by the match officials.

Fans voiced their annoyance, as did the bench.

Liverpool cult hero and temporary Fenerbahce boss Dirk Kuyt ultimately faced a booking for his complaints.

He shook hands with Turpin before a card was shown as a sign of respect.

The Dutchman seemingly noting that his complaints went too far, but he was well within his rights to do so.

When Liverpool took the lead, it felt as if that would be the start of an easy evening for the away side.

Instead, it sparked the hosts into life and saw them get back into the game almost immediately.

The issue is, that shouldn't have been allowed to happen.

It was all down to the failings of Jeremy Jacquet as part of the Reds' wall.

He turned his back, the ball deflected off his midriff and completely wrong-footed Alisson.

The Brazilian was left raging by the centre-back and wasn't afraid to vent his frustration.

There is no hiding from just how superb the atmosphere was within Sukru Saracoglu Stadium.

It is not a nice place to play as the home fans certainly act as a 12th man.

That shouldn't come as part of a rule break, but it seems it may have.

FIFA regulations say that fans aren't allowed to bring whistles into stadiums.

"Electronic, mechanical or manual devices that produce noise or other excessively loud sounds, such as vuvuzelas, whistles, loudspeakers, etc. Heaters for drums are also prohibited."

There has been suggestions that Fenerbahce supporters were blowing whistles throughout the encounter, which breaches these rules.

It didn't necessarily have an impact on proceedings, but still raises a question for Liverpool.

#2034. GdS: Why Milan and Inter are expected to bench their most in-form players

Alphadjo Cisse and Carlo Augusto are both expected to start on the bench in tonight’s Derby della Madonnina, despite being among the best players for AC Milan and Inter so far.

For Milan, tonight’s derby is a chance to extend their unbeaten run in the fixture and to decrease the gap in the standings. For Inter, it’s a chance to end the winless run and to truly assert themselves against the Rossoneri, with +10 in sight.

Read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

In other words, it’s a very important game and the tactical battle is expected to play an important role in the outcome. Team selection is thus top of mind for Ruben Amorim and Cristian Chivu who, however, are looking to bench a couple of their best players: Cisse and Augusto.

Starting with Cisse, as Gazzetta dello Sport highlights, Amorim’s decision is both tactical and psychological. He fears that there will be too much pressure on the youngster’s shoulders, while the plan is also to play with a 4-4-1-1 that can turn into a 4-3-3 or a 4-2-3-1 depending on the moment.

In that sense, Amorim believes Diego Moreira and Christian Pulisic are better suited to playing out wide than Cisse. More specifically, they arre better suited to playing out wide when not in possession, where Inter will push hard.

Playing with attacking-minded midfielders like Moreira and Pulisic, plus a trequartista like Cisse behind Goncalo Ramos (i.e. a 4-2-3-1), would result in an unbalanced team. Behind Ramos there will be Rabiot, who, when not in possession, will act as a central midfielder.

Therefore, Cisse will start on the bench and be used as needed in the second half.

Moving on to Augusto, over the past two months, he has saved Inter on numerous occasions: the assist that started the comeback against Napoli, the goal in Madrid, the turnaround goal against Bologna, and the decisive blow in the Champions League against Shakhtar.

The latest contribution was the own goal he forced against Venezia, which Chivu’s men used to seal a game that could have gone terribly wrong. Yet, in tonight’s derby against Milan, the Brazilian could start on the bench.

The battle with Federico Dimarco will be decided in the final hours, but the reality is that the Italian is still considered the starter on the left. As such, it’s a question of hierarchy, though we will likely see the player come off the bench either way.

Everton are concerned that their lack of striker depth could prompt Minnesota United to increase their asking price for Kelvin Yeboah, sources have told Football Insider.

The Toffees are clear admirers of the 26-year-old, who has netted 18 goals from just 32 games in the MLS so far this season.

The Merseysiders are desperate to bring in a new frontman in January to ensure that they get support for Thierno Barry in the second half of the season.

However, sources say that they are caught in a "catch-22" situation, where clubs are likely to increase their asking price for Everton targets, knowing that they may have little choice but to pay.

That scenario is likely to play out when it comes to Yeboah, given that the former Genoa man is on the radar of a whole host of European clubs.

Everton are keen to give him the chance to impress in the Premier League, but they may have to stump up significant cash in order to get him.

Yeboah hasn't played in European football since 2024, but he already has Premier League pedigree running through his family.

The former Italy U21 international is the nephew of former Leeds United forward Tony Yeboah, who netted 24 Premier League goals across two full campaigns for the Whites in the mid 1990s

Everton are hoping that their lack of depth at the top of the pitch can work in their favour this winter, as any targets know that they will effectively be guaranteed minutes.

David Moyes knows that he cannot only rely on Barry for the entire season, as he has no injury cover for him at the moment.

Tempting Yeboah into the move is not likely to be an issue for Everton, but dealing with a possible change of price tag could prove trickier.

Former Everton chief executive Keith Wyness told Football Insider earlier this week that Amanda Staveley's chances of buying the club have "increased" now that Michael Dell has ruled himself out of the running.

Recent reports have suggested that Staveley's PCP Partners company have already held talks with Everton regarding a potential deal.

However, Wyness believes that the former Newcastle investor still has "questions" to answer before she can proceed.

Staveley's backers for any potential bid are currently unclear, and Wyness feels that they must be revealed before she can have a genuine chance of taking over.

#2031. Liverpool lead twice before losing to Fenerbahce in Champions League

Even Liverpool’s multi-million pound bench could not rescue a team floundering in Istanbul as a chaotic performance was punished by Fenerbahce as they twice came from behind to win 3-2.

Alexander Isak had scored within three minutes of coming on to put the visitors ahead going into the final quarter but, like in the first half, the lead lasted just four minutes before former West Brom trainee Archie Brown equalised courtesy of some lax defending.

But worse was to follow as Vedat Muriqi outjumped three players to nod in the winner and end Liverpool’s 100 per cent record.

And while Andoni Iraola will be scrutinised for making five changes, including resting three of his front four in Sunday’s defeat to Arsenal, it was the way the team lost their cool and control in a game they had in hand which was more damaging.

It was a harsh result on 19-year-old Trey Nyoni, who belied his relative inexperience with a composed performance capped by an excellent volley to open the scoring, becoming Liverpool’s youngest player to register his maiden goal in the Champions League and second-youngest scorer in the competition after Trent Alexander-Arnold.

But Liverpool’s Turkish troubles continued – they lost twice to Galatasaray last season – on a typically fractious night in Istanbul, with former Manchester United forward Mason Greenwood scoring the first equaliser with a free-kick which deflected in off Jeremy Jacquet.

They had been in total command up to that point but from there the game descended into something more manic, which suited a team hammered 6-0 at Villa Park last month and stoked a febrile home crowd.

Hearts get bad news on Calvin Miller in latest injury blow ‘I hold my hands up’ - McAvennie issues fresh apology to Celtic star Auston Trusty

Many of Liverpool’s players did not cope well in that atmosphere but, to his immense credit, Nyoni shone.

Iraola’s choice to leave out Isak, Florian Wirtz and Cody Gakpo as they come to the end of a run of nine games in 27 days was understandable but it left his side toothless.

Bradley Barcola was deployed as striker but his unfamiliarity with the role was evident after failing to properly anticipate Joe Gomez’s low cross to the near post.

He did flick one header wide but struggled with the physicality of Fenerbahce’s centre-backs, even though Kojo Oppong was making his first Champions League start.

There was a lot of naivety within the visitors’ ranks – Victor Munoz snatched at an early chance when he was found in acres of space before redeeming himself by eventually forcing Ederson into a save – but none of it came from Nyoni.

The teenager was composed on just his seventh Champions League appearance – with everything going through him at the base of midfield.

His use of the ball, tactical awareness and unshakeable belief in his own ability meant amid the hurly burly of a typically Turkish clash he was head and shoulders above everyone else.

Even the usually unflappable Virgil van Dijk’s patience was tested, pushing Irfan Kahveci to the floor at a second-half corner, having twice had Romelu Lukaku leave something on him in the early stages.

When Liverpool’s breakthrough came it was fully deserved as Rio Ngumoha’s cross to the far post saw Van Dijk’s pressure force Brown to head weakly to the edge of the penalty area where Nyoni dispatched the dropping ball via a deflection off Oppong.

But after a sliding Kahveci smashed against the crossbar from five yards, Greenwood’s free-kick went through the wall.

Isak headed in Gakpo’s cross with his first chance after those two and Wirtz were summoned in the 66th minute, but the unmarked Brown tapped in the equaliser and more poor defending saw Muriqi head home the winner.

#2030. 17-pass Liverpool player was ‘virtually anonymous’ v Fenerbahce; it’ll be a ‘concern’ for Iraola

One Liverpool player was accused of being ‘virtually anonymous’ in the Reds’ 3-2 defeat to Fenerbahce in the Champions League on Wednesday.

Andoni Iraola overhauled his attack for the game in Istanbul with a reshuffle which saw Bradley Barcola deployed in an unfamiliar centre-forward role as Alexander Isak began on the substitutes’ bench.

The Swedish marksman came on as part of a triple change in the 66th minute and scored with his first touch, but that goal would ultimately count for nothing as the home side struck twice more to secure victory.

Barcola stayed on the pitch for the full 90 minutes at the Sukru Saracoglu Stadium, but his performance came in for criticism from Liverpool Echo reporter Paul Gorst.

The journalist gave the France international a lowly 4/10 in his post-match player ratings as he wrote: ‘Virtually anonymous in that centre-forward role that is unfamiliar to him. Glanced one header wide. Moved wide with 25 minutes to go but still struggled. This was a concern.’

Want more Empire of the Kop coverage? Add us as a preferred source on Google to your favourites list for news you can trust

Iraola has shown that he likes his attackers to be flexible enough to play anywhere across the forward line, but the experiment of playing Barcola in the number 9 role didn’t work.

The Frenchman was unable to get on the end of a teasing cross from Joe Gomez in the way that a more natural poacher like Isak might’ve done, and he’ll feel that he should’ve done better with a glancing header shortly before half-time.

He did prompt one good save from Ederson after the interval, but on the whole the 24-year-old was disappointingly peripheral, as the figures below from Sofascore would suggest.

We fully expect Isak to be restored at centre-forward for the visit to Crystal Palace on Sunday, but it’ll be interesting to see whether Barcola reverts to a wide role or is omitted from the starting XI after a subdued display tonight.

On this evidence, we don’t envisage him being asked to lead the line again any time soon.
